§ 862-864 ]                   SYNTAX.                         503

§ 862. The Genitive is used with' indeclinables like अरे, वारे, छते, &c.; गङ्गाया मध्ये पूरे वा in the middle or on the other side of the Ganges; अमीषां प्राणानां छते for the sake of this life.

§ 863. With superlatives, and words having the sense of the superlative, the Genitive is used; वृणां ब्राह्मण: श्रेष्ठ:; अग्रणीर्मुनि-छत्तगुरीणाम् ( Rag. V. 4. ) the chief of sages, the authors to the Mantras.

Note:—Words having the sense of comparatives are used with the Ablative and sometimes with the Instrumental; अय-त्रस्माद् बलेन हीन: or अधिक: this person is superior or inferior to him in strength; similarly देवदत्तो यज्ञदत्ताज्ज्ञातो वा; को ह त्वन्ततरो मया who will have a happier end than I ? The word अधिक is used with the Genitive, the Locative or the Instru-mental; इतरेषं तातामधिकोऽपि सोऽभवत् he was more ( i. e. dearer ) to them than their sons; तेषामभ्यधिका मासा: पञ्च च द्वादश क्षपा: they passed five months and twelve nights more than ( those years ); कुडवेऽधिक: प्रस्थ: A Prastha is larger than a Kudava.

THE LOCATIVE CASE.

§ 864. * The place where an action takes place with re-ference to the subject or object is called Adhikaraṇa ( आधिकरण ) and is put in the Locative case; † स्थलिति तिलिषु ( Bhaṭṭ. 1. 50); वासो मन्दनकानने ( Ibid 54 ); स्थाल्यां ओदनं पचति cooks food in a cooking utensil; कर्णे कथयति tells ( something ) into the ear; शीर्षे वेदना आदि, &c. The Locative also denotes the time when an action takes place; तस्मिन् विप्रकृता: काले विप्रोक्ष्य: ( Kum. II. 1. ) the gods being harassed at that time; दिवान्ते निष्क्रम्य ययु: ( Rag. II. 15. )
